title: Pre- and postoperative assessment of health-related quality of life in patients with hemifacial spasm using standardized questionnaires
summary:
Background
Hemifacial spasm is a rare condition in which the muscles on one side of the face repeatedly contract involuntarily. The symptoms may become more pronounced over time and can significantly affect everyday life, particularly social interactions. In most cases, the condition is caused by a blood vessel that lies directly next to the facial nerve inside the skull and irritates the nerve.

Treatment options include regular injections that temporarily relax the affected facial muscles. Another treatment option is surgery, during which the contact between the blood vessel and the facial nerve is relieved. This procedure directly addresses the underlying cause of the condition and offers the possibility of long-term improvement or complete relief of symptoms.

Research question
This study aims to investigate how the quality of life of patients with hemifacial spasm changes after surgery. In particular, the study will examine changes in physical and emotional well-being as well as participation in social life over time following surgery.

Methods
The participants’ quality of life will be assessed using standardized questionnaires. The first assessment will take place before surgery. Further assessments will be performed at three months, twelve months, and 48 months after surgery. By comparing the results at these different time points, the study aims to determine how quality of life changes in the short, medium, and long term after surgery.

interventions.name: Patients with hemifacial spasm are assessed using standardized questionnaires on health-related quality of life (HRQoL) preoperatively and at 3, 12, and 48 months after microvascular decompression (MVD; Jannetta procedure).
